Zeus.what: Zeus checks Ares with thunderbolts when he rushes to avenge Penthesileia.
Zeus forbids the gods to intervene in the slaughter and yields to Dawn's grief.
Zeus drives Ares and Athena apart with thunder, then veils Troy in cloud at Ganymede's plea.
Zeus grants Antenor's prayer of doom for Troy but keeps Neoptolemus fighting.
Zeus's thunder makes the resisting chiefs yield, and he returns in wrath to stop the gods' war.
Zeus gives Athena his weapons to wreck the Greek fleet.

Agamemnon.what: Agamemnon outraces Sthenelus on horseback in the funeral games.
Agamemnon fears Aias with Teucer and promises protection after Aias's death.
Agamemnon apologizes to Philoctetes with gifts and the Greeks arm for battle.

Achilles.what: Achilles kills Penthesileia, then is struck by her beauty and regrets it.
Achilles duels Memnon and kills him.
Defying Apollo, Achilles is shot in the ankle, fights on and dies.
Achilles' funeral games are held in his honour.
Achilles' arms are the prize contested by Aias and Odysseus.
Achilles' ghost demands Polyxeina's sacrifice, threatening storms.

Diomedes.what: Diomedes is angry at Achilles for killing his kinsman Thersites.
Tydeides wrestles Aias to an even match until Nestor stops them.
Diomedes rejects Menelaus' proposal to flee and sails to Scyros.
Diomede helps persuade Neoptolemus to leave Scyros and come to Troy.
Diomedes goes to Lemnos and brings Philoctetes back.
Diomedes kills Coroebus and Ilioneus in the sack.

Odysseus.what: Odysseus, wounded, helps defend Achilles' body.
Odysseus contends with Aias for Achilles' arms and wins them.
Ulysses goes to Lemnos and brings Philoctetes back.
Ulysses proposes the Horse stratagem and urges the chiefs into ambush.
Odysseus opens the Horse and leads the chiefs out.

Nestor.what: Nestor calls Achilles to face Memnon after Antilochus' death.
Nestor sings of Thetis' wedding and shames the young into boxing.
Nestor persuades the kings to let Trojan captives judge the arms.
Nestor consoles Podaleirius with words of shared sorrow and Fate.
Nestor is refused entry into the Horse.

Neoptolemus.what: Neoptolemus leaves Scyros, drives Eurypylus' men from the wall and mourns in Achilles' tent.
Neoptolemus kills Eurypylus in single combat and drives Trojans behind their walls.
Neoptolemus confronts Deiphobus and rallies the Greeks against the Scaean Gate.
Neoptolemus beheads Priam at the altar.
Neoptolemus slays Polyxeina at his father's tomb.

Aias.what: Aias defends Achilles' body and wounds Paris with a stone.
Aias wrestles Tydeides and wins Memnon's arms with the iron bar.
Aias loses the arms, is driven mad by Athena, slaughters sheep and kills himself.
Aias is wounded by Aeneas' stone as Eurypylus routs the Greeks.

Thetis.what: Thetis mourns Achilles with the Nereids and receives Poseidon's promise of an island.
Thetis arrives and sets out prizes for the funeral games.
Thetis displays Achilles' arms and rages with the Nereids at Aias' fate.
Thetis speeds the Greek ships from Tenedos to Troy.

Athena.what: Athena aids Neoptolemus in driving Eurypylus' men from the wall.
Athena confronts Ares until Zeus's thunder drives both away.
Athena softens Philoctetes' wrath and restores him.
Athena inspires the Horse and blinds Laocoon, sending serpents against his sons.
Athena takes Zeus's weapons and wrecks the Greek fleet.

Priam.what: Priam welcomes Penthesileia and prays to Zeus as an eagle seizes a dove.
Priam debates in council and feasts Memnon.
Priam is beheaded at the altar by Achilles' son.

Aeneas.what: Aeneas urges the Trojans to fight in the open field.
Aeneas, roused by Apollo, is carried off by Aphrodite, then smashes the Greek shield-roof.
Aeneas escapes Troy carrying his father and leading his son.

Paris.what: Paris insults Polydamas in the council of despair.
Paris urges the Trojans to drag off Achilles' body and is wounded by Aias.
Philoctetes wounds Paris, Oenone refuses him, and he dies on Ida.

Apollo.what: Apollo warns Achilles, then shoots him in the ankle.
Apollo snatches the Lycian hero Glaucus from his pyre.
Apollo hides Deiphobus in cloud and descends to aid Troy.
Disguised as Polymestor, Apollo inspires Aeneas and Eurymachus.
Apollo helps Poseidon flood away the Greeks' wall.

Helen.what: Helen mourns Paris, more for herself.
Helen is found by Menelaus and spared.
Helen walks ashamed and begs Menelaus' pardon; he forgives her.

Idomeneus.what: Idomeneus wins the boxing by default.

Menelaus.what: Menelaus tests the Greeks with talk of flight and promises Hermione.
Menelaus kills Deiphobus and is disarmed by Aphrodite on finding Helen.
Menelaus forgives Helen and embraces her.

Teucer.what: Teucer rallies the Argives against Eurypylus.

Ares.what: Ares rushes to avenge his daughter Penthesileia and is stopped by Zeus.
Ares secretly helps Troy until Athena and Zeus drive him off.
Ares fights in the gods' war by the Xanthus.

Calchas.what: Calchas urges that Achilles' son be fetched.
Calchas declares Troy cannot fall without Philoctetes.
Calchas reads an omen guiding the Horse plan.
Calchas forbids the Greeks to harm Aeneas.
Calchas warns in vain of disaster.

Deiphobus.what: Deiphobus rallies Troy and slaughters Greeks until Neoptolemus confronts him.

Eurypylus.what: Eurypylus arrives, takes up Hercules' shield, and kills Nireus and Machaon.
Eurypylus slays Peneleos and drives the Greeks behind their wall.
Neoptolemus kills Eurypylus in single combat.

Hera.what: Hera angrily reproaches Apollo for killing Achilles.
Hera reproaches Zeus for helping Troy.

Podaleirius.what: Podaleirius wants to die at his brother Machaon's tomb.

Aphrodite.what: Aphrodite carries her son Aeneas off the battlefield.
Aphrodite guides Aeneas out and disarms Menelaus.

Epeius.what: Epeius builds the Wooden Horse after Athena's dream.
Epeius helps Odysseus open the Horse.

Meriones.what: Meriones kills Phylodamas with an arrow at the gates.

Philoctetes.what: Philoctetes is found wasted on Lemnos, healed, and reconciled with Agamemnon.
Philoctetes wounds Paris with Hercules' arrows.
Philoctetes trades taunts with Aeneas at the walls.

Phoenix.what: Phoenix weeps over Neoptolemus in Achilles' tent.

Polydamas.what: Polydamas urges returning Helen and is insulted by Paris.

Andromache.what: Andromache sees Astyanax hurled from the tower and is enslaved.

Antenor.what: Antenor prays to Zeus to end Troy's suffering.

Pallas.what: Pallas sends Penthesileia a false dream in the shape of her father.

Briseis.what: Briseis laments over Achilles' washed body.

Cassandra.what: Cassandra prophesies ruin and tries to burn the Horse.
Cassandra is outraged in Athena's temple by Aias.

Poseidon.what: Poseidon promises Thetis that Achilles will live on an island.
Poseidon forbids Apollo to kill Neoptolemus.
Poseidon buries Aias under a rock and floods the Greek wall.

Sinon.what: Sinon deceives the Trojans with his false tale.
Sinon raises the torch to signal the fleet.

Acamas.what: Acamas finds his grandmother Aethra and takes her to safety.

Aeolus.what: Aeolus looses the winds and shatters the Greek fleet.

Aias, son of Oileus.what: Aias son of Oileus wins the footrace.
Aias son of Oileus outrages Cassandra in Athena's temple.

Glaucus.what: Apollo rescues Glaucus from his pyre, and a stream honours him.

Hecuba.what: Hecuba is changed into a hound and then stone.

Helenus.what: Helenus recognises Ares and rallies the Trojans.

Iris.what: Iris is sent by Athena to Aeolus.

Penthesileia.what: Penthesileia arrives at Troy and vows to kill Achilles.
Penthesileia drives the Greeks back until Achilles kills her.

Themis.what: Themis persuades the quarrelling gods to stop their strife after Zeus returns in wrath.

Aethra.what: Aethra, enslaved to Helen, is found by her grandsons Demophoon and Acamas and taken to safety.

Agapenor.what: Agapenor wins the leaping contest at Achilles' funeral games.

Alcimedon.what: Alcimedon is killed by Aeneas while climbing a ladder in the assault on the walls.

Anchises.what: Anchises is carried out of burning Troy on his son Aeneas' back.

Astyanax.what: Astyanax is hurled from the tower by the Greeks and dies.

Calliope.what: Calliope urges Thetis to bear her grief as the Muses mourn Achilles.

Coroebus.what: Coroebus, Cassandra's suitor, is killed by Diomedes during the sack.

Cymothoe.what: Cymothoe and the Nereids rage at Prometheus as Aias lies stunned.

Eos.what: Eos watches her son Memnon fall to Achilles.
Dawn mourns Memnon, threatens darkness, then yields to Zeus.

Deidameia.what: Deidameia fears for Neoptolemus and pleads with him as he leaves Scyros.

Demophoon.what: Demophoon and Acamas find their grandmother Aethra and take her to safety.

Electra.what: Electra, the Pleiad, hides herself during the sack of Troy.

Eurymachus.what: Eurymachus, inspired by Apollo, joins Aeneas in driving the Greeks back.

Ganymede.what: Ganymede pleads for his homeland and Zeus veils Troy in cloud.

Ilioneus.what: Old Ilioneus is killed by Diomedes despite his plea.

Laocoon.what: Laocoon warns against the Horse and is blinded by Athena.
Serpents sent by Athena kill Laocoon's sons.

Laodice.what: Laodice, Priam's daughter, is swallowed by the earth.

Lycomedes.what: Lycomedes warns Neoptolemus of the sea as he departs from Scyros.

Memnon.what: Memnon is feasted by Priam and receives the heirloom cup.
Memnon kills Antilochus, spares Nestor and routs the Argives.
Memnon duels Achilles and is killed.
Memnon's body is carried away and his Aethiopians become birds.

Nauplius.what: Nauplius lures Greek ships onto the rocks with a false torch.

Oenone.what: Oenone scornfully refuses to heal wounded Paris and drives him away to Helen.
Oenone runs through the night and leaps onto Paris's pyre, burning with him.

Polyxeina.what: Polyxeina is sacrificed at Achilles' tomb and buried by Antenor.

Tecmessa.what: Tecmessa mourns Aias with Teucer after he kills himself.

Theano.what: Theano persuades the Trojan women, urged by Tisiphone, to stay home instead of fighting.

Thersites.what: Thersites mocks Achilles' pity for Penthesileia and Achilles kills him with one blow.

Thymoetes.what: Thymoetes debates with Priam and Polydamas whether to flee, hold the walls or return Helen.

Tisiphone.what: Tisiphone urges the Trojan women to fight but is stopped by Theano.
